title: AM, GM and inequalities
examples: When can I use the AM-GM inequality?
What is the difference between the arithmetic mean and geometric mean?
Can I use this inequality for variables that can be negative?

explain.say: Today we look at three means for numbers. You will learn about the arithmetic mean and the geometric mean.
The arithmetic mean is simply the average of a set of numbers. You add them all up and then divide by the count.
For two positive numbers, the geometric mean is the square root of their product. You multiply them and then take the square root.
A key relationship is that the arithmetic mean is always greater than or equal to the geometric mean. This is the AM-GM inequality.

items: or equal to the geometric mean

explain.say: For example, if the numbers are two and eight, the AM is five. The GM is four. Five is greater than four.

faq.q: When can I use the AM-GM inequality?
faq.a: You can use it when you need to find a minimum or maximum value for a product, given a fixed sum. It works best with positive numbers.
asks: What kind of problem needs AM-GM?

faq.q: What is the difference between the arithmetic mean and geometric mean?
faq.a: The arithmetic mean uses simple addition and division. The geometric mean uses multiplication and then taking the root.
asks: How are AM and GM different?
Do I add or multiply for GM?

faq.q: Does the inequality always hold true?
faq.a: Yes, for positive numbers, the arithmetic mean is always greater than or equal to the geometric mean. They are only equal if all the numbers are the same.
asks: Is AM always bigger than GM?
When are AM and GM equal?

faq.q: Can I use this inequality if some numbers are zero?
faq.a: If any of the numbers are zero, the geometric mean will be zero. The inequality still holds true in that case.
asks: What if one number is zero?

faq.q: What if the numbers are negative?
faq.a: The standard AM-GM inequality is designed for positive real numbers. You should be careful applying it to negative numbers.
asks: Can I use this with negative numbers?
Is it okay if the numbers are less than zero?

facts: The arithmetic mean of two numbers a and b is (a plus b) divided by two.
The geometric mean of two positive numbers a and b is the square root of (a times b).
The AM-GM inequality states that the arithmetic mean is greater than or equal to the geometric mean.
Equality in the AM-GM inequality holds only when all the numbers are identical.

quiz.why: The product is fixed at 9, and the AM-GM inequality helps find the minimum sum, not the product itself. The product is always 9.

quiz.why: The arithmetic mean is found by adding the numbers and dividing by two: (4 plus 16) divided by two equals 10.
